title: Prediction-engine unit tests (computeItemStats fixtures)
goal: computeItemStats (lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts:241) is the pure function the entire cadence/prediction feature is built on, and docs/MANUAL-TESTS.md already has three hand-computed fixtures (S-14a/b/c) recorded as the algorithm's own acceptance criteria -- converting those to unit tests is free, high-signal regression coverage for the riskiest logic in the app.
in_scope: lib/predictions/computeItemStats.test.ts, three fixture-driven tests matching docs/MANUAL-TESTS.md's E-5 section verbatim: day 0/7/14/21 purchases -> bucket=weekly, confidence ~0.50, next-purchase ~day 28 (S-14c fixture 1).
day 0/7/60/67 -> the 60-day outlier is rejected, bucket stays weekly (S-14c fixture 2).
A same-Kolkata-day duplicate purchase (two events on the same calendar day in Asia/Kolkata) collapses into one event before interval math runs, not a spurious ~0-day interval (S-14a).

Read computeItemStats.ts's exported _internal (line 283) if any of the above requires exercising a sub-step directly rather than only the top-level export -- prefer testing the public computeItemStats API first, drop to _internal only if a fixture can't be expressed through it alone.
out_of_scope: S-14b's rate-blended next-purchase-date fixture (needs quantity-reliability data not covered by MANUAL-TESTS.md's recorded fixtures for S-14c) and the perishability-clamp fixture -- both real gaps, logged as a follow-up rather than inventing untested-in-production expected values.
recompute.ts / reconcile.ts (the DB-touching callers) -- those are S-45's concern, not this story's.
acceptance: Unit tests reproduce the three MANUAL-TESTS.md S-14a/b/c fixtures verbatim: day 0/7/14/21 purchases bucket weekly with confidence ~0.50 and next-purchase ~day 28; day 0/7/60/67 rejects the 60-day outlier and stays weekly; a 2-purchase item is prior-dominated with confidence ~0.25 and bucket=unpredictable. A same-Kolkata-day duplicate purchase collapses into one event before interval math runs.
invariants: Tests assert against computeItemStats's actual exported types (lib/predictions/types.ts) -- no `any`, no loosely-typed fixture objects.
Fixture dates are literal ISO strings matching MANUAL-TESTS.md's own day-0/7/14/21 framing, not derived from `new Date()` (must be deterministic, no flakiness from run-time clock).
